plan.title: installer: one read-only API for what Directive owns in a project (ownership record + per-file 'Directive-only change' check)

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan unit P2-U0 (story id ovpr-p2-u0), spec units/P2-U0-publish-ownership-record-api.md. A new read-only module, packages/core/src/install-health/owned-paths.ts, lists what Directive owns in a project (listDirectiveOwnedPaths) and says whether a file change is Directive-only (classifyDirectiveOwnedChange). Setup also records the four deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs hook files in GENERATION.json, and both uninstallers learn to match the .mjs hook command, so uninstall removes the registrations and then the files. The commit gate (P4-U1), doctor and uninstall read this API later instead of keeping their own lists.
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

Directive writes files into every project: hook files, hook settings, git hooks, skill pointers, a block in `AGENTS.md`, lines in `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes`, and its own dependency line in `package.json` and the lockfile. Several parts of Directive need to know exactly which changes are Directive's own: uninstall (to remove them), doctor (to warn about them), the commit gate (to let them through), and the `.gitattributes` cleanup.

Today each part keeps its own hand-written list. The lists disagree, and all of them are incomplete. The most visible result: a person or agent cannot commit Directive's own refreshed files without a planning brief (#5771, #5944, #5949). A second result: uninstall does not recognise the current hook files at all.

Evidence (origin/master `def527f5e`):
- The record exists and is written on every setup. Format, reader and writer: `packages/core/src/install-health/ownership.ts` (`GENERATION_REL` `:26`; `parseOwnershipRecord` `:193`, which rejects the whole record on an unknown kind; `readOwnershipRecord` `:316`). Writer: `buildOwnershipArtifacts` in `packages/runtime/src/setup.ts:276`, called from `runSetup` (`:486`).
- Not in the record:
  - the hook `.mjs` outers (`deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs`, four hosts), written by `ensureHostHooks` (`packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts:1010`);
  - the managed `.gitignore` lines (`setup.ts:166-168`);
  - the managed `.gitattributes` lines (`ensureManagedPathGitattributes`, `setup-wiring.ts:480`);
  - the managed `.prettierignore` line;
  - the `package.json` dependency entry and the lockfile entries.
- Other hand-kept lists, none of which reads the record:
  - `MANAGED_HOOK_DEPOSIT_REL_PATHS` / `isLifecycleOrInstallerRelPath` in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:5598-5615` (the commit gate);
  - `installerManagedMatchers()` in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/hygiene.ts:100` (retired deft-core-guard, #5835);
  - `INSTALLER_OUTPUT_INVENTORY` in `packages/runtime/src/installer-output-inventory.ts` (prose, not a machine list).
- Uninstall defect (found by reading, not by running): both `isManagedHookCommand` functions (`packages/runtime/src/uninstall.ts:76-84`, `packages/cli/src/uninstall-map.ts:447-454`) test `/(^|[\s"`'])deft-hook([\s"`']|$)/`. The registered command is `node .claude/deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs …`. The character before `deft-hook` is `/` and the one after is `-`, so it never matches. Setup's own matcher uses `isHostHookOuterCommand` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts:66-67`). After uninstall, the registrations and the `.mjs` files stay and point at a removed runtime (AC11.4, AC11.11).
- Reusable content-aware helpers already exist in `hygiene.ts` (#3193): `isDirectiveDependencyKey` (`:345`), `isUpgradePinPathContentAllowed` (`:809`) and the lockfile follow-through checks it calls.

## What the design says

- AC11.10: the committed ownership record "identifies wholly owned files, Directive-owned marked sections or structured entries in shared files, and settings/data that survive uninstall." The launcher treats it as bounded cleanup information, "never authority to delete arbitrary paths or user content."
- §A6.1: `GENERATION.json` holds ownership and removal information. "Representation is an implementation detail, not a generic installer framework."
- AC11.2, AC11.4: uninstall uses the record and the launcher's known-layout map; no owned registration may remain that targets a deleted file.
- AC3.1 / AC3.3: the launcher may know the record and the uninstall map, but has no runtime or core dependency.
- AC8.5: setup adds only the `node_modules` and readiness-marker ignore lines.
- AC12.1: doctor writes nothing, so anything doctor calls must be a pure read.
- D-001 (Rule 2): the commit gate reads the installer's ownership record, not a hand-kept list. polfer publishes the record (this ticket); Scott's gate reads it (P4-U1, #5771).
- D-026: class 4 uses `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange` (P2-U14).
- D-027: the `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` row in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is not Directive-owned. Leave it out.

## Expected

1. **Record the `.mjs` outers.** `buildOwnershipArtifacts` adds a `whole-file` entry for each host outer on disk at `hostHookOuterRelPath(host, hostHookOuterSha8())`. No new ownership kind.
2. **Fix both uninstall matchers in the same PR.** Add `isHostHookOuterCommand` to `runtime/src/uninstall.ts`. Add the same regex inline to `cli/src/uninstall-map.ts` (the launcher can't import core). Add the `.mjs` pattern for all four hosts to `discoverKnownArtifacts`, so a missing record still finds them. Without this step, step 1 makes uninstall delete the `.mjs` files while their registrations stay.
3. **New module `packages/core/src/install-health/owned-paths.ts`** (pure, read-only), exported from `install-health/index.ts`:
   - `listDirectiveOwnedPaths(projectRoot)`: the committed record plus the runtime's known Directive path classes. Each entry has `path` (or `pattern`), `kind` (`whole-file`, `marked-section`, `structured-entry`, `managed-lines`, `dependency-entry`, `retired`, `retained`), `mustCommit` (false only for readiness markers) and `source` (`record` or `known`).
   - `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange(relPath, before, after)` → `"directive-only" | "mixed" | "not-owned"`. Rules:
     - `whole-file` and the `.mjs` pattern (any sha8, any of the four host directories): `directive-only` for create, modify or delete.
     - `retired` (Grok `.sh` wrapper, `.githooks/_deft-run.sh`, `.deft-version` markers): `directive-only` only on deletion.
     - `AGENTS.md`: compare with the managed section removed from both sides.
     - Host configs: compare with Directive's hook entries removed; invalid JSON is `mixed`.
     - `Taskfile.yml`: compare with the `deft:` include removed; a new file equal to setup's minimal Taskfile is `directive-only`.
     - `managed-lines`: compare as line multisets after removing Directive's known lines.
     - `dependency-entry`: delegate to `isUpgradePinPathContentAllowed`; handle a new `package.json` or lockfile explicitly (the #5771 first-install case).
     - Anything else: `not-owned`.
   - Safety rule: a record entry counts only if its path is inside a known Directive path class. A record entry outside those classes (for example `src/app.ts`) is ignored and reported (AC11.10).
4. **Use it in the runtime uninstaller now.** `runtime/src/uninstall.ts` builds its fallback lists from `listDirectiveOwnedPaths` instead of its local constants. The launcher keeps its own copy (AC3.1); a test compares the launcher's known-map paths with `listDirectiveOwnedPaths` on the same fixture.
5. Leave `installerManagedMatchers()` alone (it belongs to #5835). Add a comment that points to the new API.

Must not do: no new kind value in `GENERATION.json` (an older runtime would reject the whole record); no writes of any kind (doctor will call this); don't widen `.gitignore`; don't edit `dispatcher.ts` (the gate change is P4-U1); don't trust the record for arbitrary paths; no generic installer registry.

Open unit questions (the unit ships with the recommended answer unless polfer says otherwise):
- Q1: shared-file lines and dependency entries stay as code knowledge in the API, not in `GENERATION.json`. (Putting them in the record would change uninstall behaviour.)
- Q2: whole Directive files pass by path alone in v1. An optional byte check for the `.mjs` outer only.
- Q3b: `.deft/hook-gate-off.json` is per-clone state, not owned for commit purposes.

If the PR must split: P2-U0a = steps 3 and 5 (API only, no behaviour change); P2-U0b = steps 1, 2 and 4. P2-U0b never merges without step 2.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After `directive install` in a fixture, `GENERATION.json` lists every `deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs` that setup wrote, as `whole-file`.
2. `listDirectiveOwnedPaths(root)` returns: hook `.mjs`, host configs, `.githooks/*`, `GENERATION.json`, `data-schema.json`, the `AGENTS.md` block, skill pointers, slash wrappers, managed `.gitignore` / `.gitattributes` / `.prettierignore` lines, `package.json` / lockfile dependency entries, and readiness markers with `mustCommit: false`.
3. `listDirectiveOwnedPaths` and `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange` perform no file or git writes (tested on a read-only fixture directory).
4. `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange` returns the documented result for each test case: new `package.json` from install; `package.json` with an extra user script (`mixed`); `pnpm-lock.yaml` follow-through; `AGENTS.md` with user edits outside the block (`mixed`); `.claude/settings.json` with a user hook added (`mixed`); `.cursor/hooks/consumer-custom.mjs` (`not-owned`); old-sha8 `.mjs` deletion (`directive-only`).
5. A record entry outside the known Directive path classes is ignored.
6. `directive uninstall` on a current install removes all `.mjs` registrations before removing the `.mjs` files, and reports none left (AC11.4). Same through the launcher fallback with the record deleted.
7. Running setup twice with no change leaves `GENERATION.json` byte-identical.

Verification: `pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/install-health packages/runtime/src/uninstall.test.ts packages/cli/src/uninstall-bookend.test.ts packages/runtime/src/setup`, and `task check` on the PR.

## Related

- #5771, #5944, #5949: the commit gate reads this API in P4-U1 (Scott). Comment on each when this lands.
- #6006: a correct owned-file list for the "Review and commit" output (that presenter fix stays in #6006).
- #6007, #5999: uninstall lane (P2-U7). The `.mjs` uninstall defect is fixed here; #<uninstall .mjs ticket> if filed, else a comment on #6007.
- #5835: retired deft-core-guard (`installerManagedMatchers`).
- #6616, #6618: readers of this API.

## Plan placement

- Unit P2-U0, story id `ovpr-p2-u0`. Phase 2, wave 2.1. Size M.
- Depends on: nothing.
- Blocks: P2-U14 (class 4), P4-U1 (commit gate), P3-U2b (doctor hidden-file warning), P2-U5 (attributes cleanup).

admitted_source_sentences: Problem Directive writes files into every project: hook files, hook settings, git hooks, skill pointers, a block in `AGENTS.md`, lines in `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes`, and its own dependency line in `package.json` and the lockfile.

Several parts of Directive need to know exactly which changes are Directive's own: uninstall (to remove them), doctor (to warn about them), the commit gate (to let them through), and the `.gitattributes` cleanup.
Today each part keeps its own hand-written list.
The lists disagree, and all of them are incomplete.
The most visible result: a person or agent cannot commit Directive's own refreshed files without a planning brief (#5771, #5944, #5949).
A second result: uninstall does not recognise the current hook files at all.
Evidence (origin/master `def527f5e`): - The record exists and is written on every setup.

Format, reader and writer: `packages/core/src/install-health/ownership.ts` (`GENERATION_REL` `:26`; `parseOwnershipRecord` `:193`, which rejects the whole record on an unknown kind; `readOwnershipRecord` `:316`).
Writer: `buildOwnershipArtifacts` in `packages/runtime/src/setup.ts:276`, called from `runSetup` (`:486`).

Not in the record: - the hook `.mjs` outers (`deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs`, four hosts), written by `ensureHostHooks` (`packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts:1010`); - the managed `.gitignore` lines (`setup.ts:166-168`); - the managed `.gitattributes` lines (`ensureManagedPathGitattributes`, `setup-wiring.ts:480`); - the managed `.prettierignore` line; - the `package.json` dependency entry and the lockfile entries.

Other hand-kept lists, none of which reads the record: - `MANAGED_HOOK_DEPOSIT_REL_PATHS` / `isLifecycleOrInstallerRelPath` in `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:5598-5615` (the commit gate); - `installerManagedMatchers()` in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/hygiene.ts:100` (retired deft-core-guard, #5835); - `INSTALLER_OUTPUT_INVENTORY` in `packages/runtime/src/installer-output-inventory.ts` (prose, not a machine list).

Uninstall defect (found by reading, not by running): both `isManagedHookCommand` functions (`packages/runtime/src/uninstall.ts:76-84`, `packages/cli/src/uninstall-map.ts:447-454`) test `/(^|[\s"`'])deft-hook([\s"`']|$)/`.
The registered command is `node .claude/deft-hook-<sha8>.mjs …`.
The character before `deft-hook` is `/` and the one after is `-`, so it never matches.
Setup's own matcher uses `isHostHookOuterCommand` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts:66-67`).
After uninstall, the registrations and the `.mjs` files stay and point at a removed runtime (AC11.4, AC11.11).
Reusable content-aware helpers already exist in `hygiene.ts` (#3193): `isDirectiveDependencyKey` (`:345`), `isUpgradePinPathContentAllowed` (`:809`) and the lockfile follow-through checks it calls.

What the design says - AC11.10: the committed ownership record "identifies wholly owned files, Directive-owned marked sections or structured entries in shared files, and settings/data that survive uninstall." The launcher treats it as bounded cleanup information, "never authority to delete arbitrary paths or user content." - §A6.1: `GENERATION.json` holds ownership and removal information.

"Representation is an implementation detail, not a generic installer framework." - AC11.2, AC11.4: uninstall uses the record and the launcher's known-layout map; no owned registration may remain that targets a deleted file.
AC3.1 / AC3.3: the launcher may know the record and the uninstall map, but has no runtime or core dependency.
AC8.5: setup adds only the `node_modules` and readiness-marker ignore lines.
AC12.1: doctor writes nothing, so anything doctor calls must be a pure read.
D-001 (Rule 2): the commit gate reads the installer's ownership record, not a hand-kept list.
polfer publishes the record (this ticket); Scott's gate reads it (P4-U1, #5771).
D-026: class 4 uses `classifyDirectiveOwnedChange` (P2-U14).
D-027: the `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` row in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is not Directive-owned.
Leave it out.
Expected 1.
Record the `.mjs` outers. `buildOwnershipArtifacts` adds a `whole-file` entry for each host outer on disk at `hostHookOuterRelPath(host, hostHookOuterSha8())`.
No new ownership kind.
Fix both uninstall matchers in the same PR. Add `isHostHookOuterCommand` to `runtime/src/uninstall.ts`.
Add the same regex inline to `cli/src/uninstall-map.ts` (the launcher can't import core).
Add the `.mjs` pattern for all four hosts to `discoverKnownArtifacts`, so a missing record still finds them.
Without this step, step 1 makes uninstall delete the `.mjs` files while their registrations stay.

New module `packages/core/src/install-health/owned-paths.ts` (pure, read-only), exported from `install-health/index.ts`: - `listDirectiveOwnedPaths(projectRoot)`: the committed record plus the runtime's known Directive path classes.

Each entry has `path` (or `pattern`), `kind` (`whole-file`, `marked-section`, `structured-entry`, `managed-lines`, `dependency-entry`, `retired`, `retained`), `mustCommit` (false only for readiness markers) and `source` (`record` or `known`).
`classifyDirectiveOwnedChange(relPath, before, after)` → `"directive-only" | "mixed" | "not-owned"`.
Rules: - `whole-file` and the `.mjs` pattern (any sha8, any of the four host directories): `directive-only` for create, modify or delete.
`retired` (Grok `.sh` wrapper, `.githooks/_deft-run.sh`, `.deft-version` markers): `directive-only` only on deletion.
`AGENTS.md`: compare with the managed section removed from both sides.
Host configs: compare with Directive's hook entries removed; invalid JSON is `mixed`.
`Taskfile.yml`: compare with the `deft:` include removed; a new file equal to setup's minimal Taskfile is `directive-only`.
`managed-lines`: compare as line multisets after removing Directive's known lines.
`dependency-entry`: delegate to `isUpgradePinPathContentAllowed`; handle a new `package.json` or lockfile explicitly (the #5771 first-install case).
Anything else: `not-owned`.
Safety rule: a record entry counts only if its path is inside a known Directive path class.
A record entry outside those classes (for example `src/app.ts`) is ignored and reported (AC11.10).
Use it in the runtime uninstaller now. `runtime/src/uninstall.ts` builds its fallback lists from `listDirectiveOwnedPaths` instead of its local constants.
The launcher keeps its own copy (AC3.1); a test compares the launcher's known-map paths with `listDirectiveOwnedPaths` on the same fixture.
Leave `installerManagedMatchers()` alone (it belongs to #5835).
Add a comment that points to the new API.

Must not do: no new kind value in `GENERATION.json` (an older runtime would reject the whole record); no writes of any kind (doctor will call this); don't widen `.gitignore`; don't edit `dispatcher.ts` (the gate change is P4-U1); don't trust the record for arbitrary paths; no generic installer registry.

Open unit questions (the unit ships with the recommended answer unless polfer says otherwise): - Q1: shared-file lines and dependency entries stay as code knowledge in the API, not in `GENERATION.json`.
(Putting them in the record would change uninstall behaviour.) - Q2: whole Directive files pass by path alone in v1.
